Agentic RAG With Metadata Extraction: When It Actually Makes Sense
RAG is everywhere now. But once you ship a basic “embed → store → retrieve → answer” pipeline, you quickly hit real‑world issues:
•
Hallucinations for increased dataset
•
Old versions of documents pollute answers
•
Complex queries need multiple hops and filters, not a single vector lookup
This is where Agentic RAG + metadata extraction becomes useful: an agent decides how to retrieve and uses structured metadata (date, owner, doc type, region, version…) to laser‑focus context before generation.unstructured+1
What Is Agentic RAG (In Practice)?
Classic RAG:
1.
Embed user query
2.
Vector search over chunks
3.
Feed top‑k chunks to LLM
4.
Generate answer
This pipeline is static and one‑shot. Agentic RAG adds a controller agent that can:
•
Decide whether retrieval is even needed
•
Rewrite the query, add filters, or do multi-hop retrieval
•
Ask tools (search, SQL, other APIs) for more context
•
Validate if the context is enough and loop again if requiredkore+2
Think of it as:
“LLM + tools + memory + policies” orchestrating retrieval, not just consuming it.
Where Metadata Extraction Fits
Metadata is structured information attached to each chunk or document: {source, doc_type, department, country, valid_from, valid_to, version, tags...}
You can:
•
Extract metadata at ingest time using rules or LLMs
•
Store it alongside embeddings in the vector DB
•
Use it for filtering and ranking at query timevectorize+2
With an agentic controller, you go one step further:
•
The agent reads the user’s query
•
Extracts desired metadata filters (e.g., country='IN', doc_type='policy', valid_from&lt;=today&lt;=valid_to)
•
Builds a filtered retrieval plan dynamically
•
Iterates if results look incomplete or inconsistenttheaiautomators+1
High-Level Architecture
You can describe the architecture like this:
1.
Ingestion & Metadata Extraction
•
Raw documents → chunker
•
Metadata extractor (rules/LLM) → {doc_type, owner, country, date_range, version...}
•
Store embedding + metadata in vector DB
2. Agentic Orchestrator
•
Reads user query
•
Extracts metadata filters from the query
•
Chooses retrieval strategy (vector only, hybrid, extra tools)
•
Validates if retrieved context is enough; may loop
3. Retriever with Metadata Filters
•
similarity_search(query_embedding, filters=metadata_filters)
•
Possibly hybrid search (BM25 + vectors) plus re-rankingzilliz+1
4. Answer Generator
•
LLM gets clean, filtered context
•
Outputs answer + citations (using stored metadata)
Minimal Agent + Metadata Flow (Pseudo / Python-ish)
Assume:
•
You already have an embed(text) function
•
You use a vector DB like Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus or Elasticsearch with metadata filters
•
You use an LLM that can do tool calling / JSON output
1. Ingestion with Metadata Extraction
from typing import Dict, List def extract_metadata_with_llm(text: str) -> Dict: # Prompt LLM: "Extract department, country, doc_type, valid_from, valid_to..." schema = { "department": "string", "country": "string", "doc_type": "string", "valid_from": "date", "valid_to": "date", "version": "string" } return llm_extract(text, schema) # your wrapper def ingest_document(doc_id: str, pages: List[str]): for page_num, page_text in enumerate(pages): chunks = chunk(page_text, max_tokens=512) for idx, chunk_text in enumerate(chunks): base_meta = extract_metadata_with_llm(chunk_text) meta = { **base_meta, "doc_id": doc_id, "page": page_num, "chunk_index": idx, } vec = embed(chunk_text) vector_db.upsert( id=f"{doc_id}-{page_num}-{idx}", vector=vec, metadata=meta, text=chunk_text, )
This is where you decide what metadata you care about. Keep it small and stable.
2. Agent Extracts Filters From Query
def infer_filters_from_query(query: str) -> Dict: # Ask LLM to output structured filters only filter_schema = { "country": "string | null", "department": "string | null", "doc_type": "string | null", "valid_after": "date | null", "valid_before": "date | null", } return llm_extract(query, filter_schema)
Example: User query:
“What is the current leave policy in India for engineering team members?”
LLM might infer:
{ "country": "IN", "department": "engineering", "doc_type": "policy", "valid_after": null, "valid_before": null }
3. Agentic Retrieval Loop
def agentic_rag_answer(query: str) -> str: filters = infer_filters_from_query(query) # Build vector DB filter object, skip nulls db_filter = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if v is not None} # 1st pass retrieval query_vec = embed(query) results = vector_db.search( vector=query_vec, top_k=10, filter=db_filter, ) if not results: # fallback: relax filters db_filter.pop("department", None) results = vector_db.search( vector=query_vec, top_k=10, filter=db_filter, ) context = " ".join(r["text"] for r in results) # Let the agent decide if more retrieval is needed decision = llm( f"""You are a retrieval agent. User query: {query} Context: {context} Is this enough to answer accurately? Answer with JSON: {{ "enough": true/false, "missing": "short description" }}""" ) if not decision["enough"]: # Example of very simple second hop: refined_query = f"{query} (focus: {decision['missing']})" query_vec = embed(refined_query) more_results = vector_db.search( vector=query_vec, top_k=5, filter=db_filter, ) context += " " + " ".join(r["text"] for r in more_results) final_answer = llm( f"""You are a helpful assistant. Use ONLY the context below to answer the question. If you are unsure, say so. Question: {query} Context: {context} """ ) return final_answer
This is a minimal agentic pattern:
•
Agent infers metadata filters
•
First filtered retrieval
•
Simple self‑check
•
Optional second retrieval hop
You can grow this into LangGraph / ReAct style flows later.
When To Use Agentic RAG + Metadata Extraction
Use this pattern when:
•
You have clear dimensions to filter on
•
Country, department, product line, environment (prod/stage), version, tenant, customer segment
•
Incorrect scope is worse than “no answer”
•
Policies, legal, finance, regulated content, contracts
•
Your corpus is large and heterogeneous
•
Many products / regions / time ranges; naive semantic search is noisycodesignal+1
•
Queries are multi-step or underspecified
•
The agent can ask: “Is this HR or Engineering?” and infer filters from the texthaystack.deepset+1
“Use agents when your knowledge has dimensions; use simple RAG when it’s just a stack of pages.”
or
“Agentic RAG is for routing through a maze; basic RAG is for reading a single book.”
When Not To Do It
Skip (or postpone) agentic + metadata-heavy RAG when:
•
Corpus is small and homogeneous
•
A single product FAQ or a small internal handbook
•
You don’t have stable metadata yet
•
Labels change frequently, or no clear schema exists; you’ll just add complexity without gain
•
Latency budget is very tight
•
Multiple LLM calls (filters + decisions) might be too expensive for your use case
•
You don’t have a clear failure mode
•
If “somewhat relevant but not perfectly filtered” is fine (e.g., generic FAQ), simple RAG is easier
In those cases, start with:
•
Clean chunking
•
Good embeddings
•
Maybe basic hard-coded filters (like date range)
Only add agents + dynamic metadata extraction once you see failure patterns that this architecture can solve.
Agentic RAG with metadata extraction is worth the complexity only when you must reliably route queries to the right, well-scoped slice of a large, heterogeneous knowledge base.
